statements.statement_en: Israel should apply its sovereignty to parts of Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this harms relations with Israel's allies.
Israel should cut economic ties with hostile states, territories and organizations, including trade, money transfers and aid agencies, even if civilians there are harmed.
The Jewish character of the state should be anchored more firmly in law, even if non-Jewish citizens feel less equal.
The state should not create or fund new heritage centers for particular communities or movements — Tunisian, Moroccan, Chabad — even if their traditions fade.
It should be easier for the state to revoke the citizenship or residency of people convicted of terrorism, even if they are left stateless.
Yeshiva students should be drafted into the army or civilian service, even if this forces them to give up full-time Torah study.
Every citizen, including groups that are exempt today, should do compulsory military or civilian service, even if the army does not need all of them.
Tuition aid, daycare, tax breaks and land should go first to those who did military or national service, even if others get less.
Israel should restrict more strictly the entry and residence of foreigners, including citizens' spouses who come from the Palestinian territories, even if this separates some families.

statements.title_en: Rights of foreign workers and asylum seekers
statements.statement_en: Israel should make it harder for foreign workers and asylum seekers to stay, work or receive benefits, even if their living conditions worsen.

statements.title_en: Foreign states and international organizations in Israel
statements.statement_en: Israel should restrict more strictly the activity of foreign states and international organizations on its territory, such as UNRWA, even at the cost of conflict with the UN and allies.
Israel should reduce the number of foreign workers, even if construction, agriculture and elderly care become more expensive.
Soldiers, reservists, veterans and bereaved military families should receive more payments and benefits from the state, even if this requires raising taxes.
Conditions for prisoners jailed for terrorism should be harsher — only basic medical care, no Red Cross visits, fewer privileges — even if Israel faces international criticism.

statements.title_en: Funding schools without the core curriculum
statements.statement_en: Every school should be required to teach core subjects such as math and English, even if schools that refuse lose state funding.
Getting a divorce should be easier, even if one of the spouses objects.
The state should tighten control over non-profits funded by foreign governments, for example by taxing such donations, even if this limits independent civil-society groups.
Couples should be able to marry in Israel without a religious ceremony, even if the Chief Rabbinate does not recognize such marriages.
Elected officials should have more say over the courts, for example in appointing judges or overriding rulings, even if the courts become less independent.

statements.title_en: Separate spaces for men and women
statements.statement_en: Separating men and women should be allowed in state and municipal settings — swimming hours, events, study programs — even if this limits one sex's access at certain times.
Rabbinical courts should be allowed to hear civil and property disputes when both sides agree, even if this weakens the role of state courts.
The state should spend more on public transport, such as fare discounts and more bus lines, even if this requires raising taxes.
The state should reduce its support for settlements in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this makes life there harder for settlers.
Much more housing construction should be allowed, even at the cost of building on open spaces and greater strain on infrastructure.
Citizens should be allowed to withdraw locked savings, such as pension, study funds or child savings plans, early, even if less remains for the future.
The state should expand legal protections and equal rights for LGBT people, even if religious citizens and businesses must sometimes act against their beliefs.
The state should lower barriers to imports and new competitors, even if existing local businesses lose income.
Measures against terrorists and their supporters should be harsher, such as the death penalty or revoking citizenship, even if uninvolved people are affected.
The police and security forces should be given broader powers to arrest, search, monitor and use force, even if the risk of abuse grows.
Appointments to senior state posts should be vetted by an independent committee, even if it can block candidates chosen by elected politicians.
Suspects and defendants should have fewer legal protections during arrest, questioning and trial, even if the risk of convicting innocent people grows.
New immigrants (olim) should receive more benefits and assistance, even at the expense of other parts of the budget.

statements.title_en: Protecting the weaker party to a contract
statements.statement_en: The law should dictate more terms in contracts with consumers, tenants and borrowers, such as limits on fees, even if this restricts freedom to negotiate.
Public services should be run by state bodies rather than handed to private companies or organizations, even if this costs the budget more.
People involved in terrorism should lose state benefits and rights, such as allowances, prison conditions or state-paid lawyers, even if their families lose income.
Personal information should be better protected by law, even if this makes it harder for the police and the media to obtain it.
Parents charged with serious violence against family members should lose guardianship of their children, even before a court convicts them.
The state should have broader powers to confiscate property linked to crime or terrorism, even if innocent owners are sometimes harmed.
Ministers should have more control over appointing and directing senior officials, such as legal advisers and police chiefs, even if those officials become less independent.
The Supreme Court should have less power to cancel laws and government decisions, even if citizens have fewer ways to challenge them in court.
Knesset members, ministers, the prime minister and mayors should have no special protection from criminal investigation or indictment, even if investigations disrupt their work.
Prisoners and detainees should get more rights, such as rehabilitation programs and limits on shackling, even if this costs the prison service more.
The law should set minimum sentences for serious crimes, such as weapons offenses, even if judges cannot give lighter sentences in exceptional cases.
Public institutions such as hospitals and army bases should follow Jewish religious rules, like no leavened bread on Passover, even if non-observant people are restricted.

statements.title_en: Land purchase in Judea and Samaria
statements.statement_en: Israelis, including Jews, should be allowed to buy land in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this makes a future territorial agreement harder.
The right to equality should be written into the Basic Laws, including the Nation-State Law, even if this weakens laws favoring the state's Jewish character.
Party lists and public bodies should be required to include a minimum share of women, even if parties must drop candidates their members chose.
Unemployment benefits should cover more people, such as the self-employed, medical interns, young workers and people in job training, even if National Insurance spends more.
Students and pupils should get more state support, such as study grants, free school meals and tuition aid, even if this costs the budget more.
Police, health funds and benefit offices should have to record and explain their decisions so people can challenge them, even at extra cost.
Teachers, lecturers and public employees who express support for terrorism should be dismissed, even without a criminal conviction.
Higher education should be made more accessible — more colleges in the periphery and easier admission rules — even if academic standards may fall.
Israel should withhold Palestinian Authority tax revenues equal to its payments to people jailed for terrorism and their families, even if the Authority collapses financially.
Widows, widowers, orphans and bereaved families should get more benefits, for example equal survivors' pensions for widowers, even if this costs the budget more.
The state should give farmers more support, such as cheaper water and investment grants, even if taxpayers and consumers pay more.
Voting should be made easier for people away from home, such as soldiers and students, even if polling becomes harder to supervise.
Health funds should owe patients more services and rights, such as treatment within a set time and ambulance refunds, even if health insurance costs rise.
Municipalities should get more powers to set local rules, for example on Shabbat public transport, security and water services, even if rules differ between towns.
More people should qualify for disability, nursing-care and sick-leave benefits, for example homemakers and the self-employed, even if National Insurance and employers pay more.
The state should impose stricter environmental rules, such as a climate law, a levy on plastic bags and protection of trees and coasts, even if this raises costs for businesses and consumers.
Debtors should be better protected — for example no electricity cut-offs for unpaid bills and no travel bans over small debts — even if creditors find it harder to collect.
Security failures such as October 7 should be investigated by a state commission of inquiry, even if the government cannot choose its members.
People under a protective order for domestic violence should be electronically monitored, even before any conviction.
Old-age pensions and benefits for Holocaust survivors should be expanded, even if this costs the budget more.
The state should provide more free education, from early childhood and after-school programs to university, even if this requires more public spending.
A prime minister should be limited to two consecutive terms, even if voters lose the option to re-elect a popular leader.

statements.title_en: Checks on the prime minister's power
statements.statement_en: The prime minister should face more checks, such as limits on replacing senior officials, even if elected governments struggle to carry out their policies.

statements.title_en: Conditions on the right to vote
statements.statement_en: The right to vote should not depend on military or national service or a prison sentence, even if those who served see this as unfair.
Public bodies and building owners should have to accommodate Jewish religious observance, such as Shabbat water pumps, even if non-observant people share the cost.
Animal protection laws should be stricter, such as a ban on trawl fishing and harsher penalties for cruelty, even if farmers and fishermen lose income.
Staff working with children, patients or the elderly should face stricter requirements, such as training and a clean criminal record, even if hiring gets harder.
Public proceedings, such as court hearings and municipal council meetings, should be filmed and broadcast, even if people appearing in them lose privacy.
Adults should be allowed to buy, grow and use cannabis for personal use, even if more people, including young people, start using it.

statements.title_en: Checks on police use of force
statements.statement_en: Police use of force should face stricter checks, such as body cameras at protests and filming of water-cannon use, even if officers hesitate to act.

statements.title_en: Child safety in daycare and schools
statements.statement_en: Daycare centers and schools should face stricter safety requirements, such as cameras, protected rooms and staff vetting, even if daycare becomes more expensive.
Authorities and developers should be able to clear old neighborhoods and unsafe buildings faster, even if residents leave before receiving full compensation or new housing.
Therapy that tries to change a minor's sexual orientation should be banned, even if parents want it for their child.
Prosecutors and the Attorney General should wait several years after leaving office before they can be appointed judges, even if fewer experienced candidates are available.
Officials should be able to run for office or join private companies soon after leaving their posts, even if this risks conflicts of interest.
Israel should cooperate with international courts, such as the International Criminal Court, even if Israeli soldiers and officials may then be tried abroad.
Crimes against children should be punished more harshly and be easier to prove, even if accused people find it harder to defend themselves.
More kinds of speech should be criminal, such as denying the October 7 massacre or inciting racism, even if free speech becomes narrower.
Existing ministries, not new national authorities, should handle social problems such as poverty and trauma, even if no single body is in charge.
Domestic-violence victims should get more protection, such as recognising economic abuse and stripping a spouse's killer of property, even if the state intervenes in families.
Landlords and businesses should be forbidden to refuse tenants or customers over origin, family status or disability, even if this limits owners' freedom of choice.
Candidates and public office holders who support terror against Israel should be barred or removed, even if never convicted of a crime.
More people should be eligible for public housing, such as single mothers and women leaving shelters, even if waiting times grow for those already in line.
Fewer jobs should need a state license, and licenses should be easier to get, such as through shorter internships, even if professional standards may fall.
Fees for public services, such as hospital parking, water bills and school payments, should be cut, even if taxes must rise to cover them.
The state should give more money and discounts to religious institutions, such as synagogues, mosques, religious councils and religious schools, even if other services get less.
The state should direct more health funding to outlying and border towns, such as new emergency rooms and lower health-insurance fees, even if central regions get less.
Private companies should choose staff and directors freely, without quotas for women, people with disabilities, Arab or Haredi citizens, even if these groups stay underrepresented.
The state, universities and employers should accommodate Muslim, Christian and Druze religious practice, such as holidays and places of prayer, even if this costs more.
Schools should give more room to Jewish and Israeli heritage, such as community histories, memorial days and the flag, even if other subjects lose time.
The state should restrict more speech, such as enemy flags, foreign channels deemed a security risk or insulting officials, even if free speech narrows.

statements.title_en: Limits on what children can access
statements.statement_en: Parents, not the law, should decide what children use, such as smartphones, social media and toy guns, even if children are exposed to more risks.
The state should pay for psychological and trauma care for more people, such as reservists' families, terror victims and abused children, even if this requires raising taxes.
Ministers and Knesset members should disclose more to the Knesset and public, such as foreign ties and outside advisers, even if this slows their work.
Arab, Druze and Circassian citizens should be guaranteed jobs and seats in public bodies matching their population share, even if other candidates are passed over.
The law should cap the number of ministers, deputy ministers and paid deputy mayors, even if this makes it harder to build coalitions.

statements.title_en: Penalties for violent and sexual crime
statements.statement_en: Penalties for crimes such as violence, sexual assault, protection rackets and illegal weapons should be raised, even if more people spend longer in prison.
Seniors, people with disabilities and parents of babies should get special treatment, such as human phone answers and reserved parking, even if businesses pay more.
The state should stop funding media outlets, such as the public broadcaster Kan and Army Radio, even if fewer news outlets survive.
Conversions to Judaism recognized by the state should be performed only under the Chief Rabbinate, even if fewer people manage to convert.
Landlords should be free to raise rent and end leases as they choose, without legal limits, even if tenants have to move more often.
People should be able to retire earlier, such as women and construction workers, even if pension funds and taxpayers pay more.
The opposition in the Knesset and city councils should get guaranteed rights, such as committee seats and chairs, even if the majority governs less freely.
Businesses and schools that discriminate should pay higher compensation or lose state funding, even if claims can succeed without proof of actual harm.
Tobacco and smoking products should face stricter limits, such as bans on advertising and flavors, even if adult smokers have fewer choices.
Homes built without a permit should be legalized or connected to electricity and water, even if this encourages more building without permits.

statements.title_en: Use of organs and sperm after death
statements.statement_en: After death, a person's organs or sperm may be used for transplants or having children unless they objected, even if they never explicitly agreed.
Welfare allowances, such as income support and the work grant for low earners, should be higher, even if this requires raising taxes.
Single people and same-sex couples should be allowed to adopt children on the same terms as married couples, even if this contradicts religious tradition.
The state should add more to people's pension and savings funds, such as tax breaks and deposits for reservists, even if taxes rise.
A regular Knesset majority should be able to change Basic Laws or override them with ordinary laws, even if basic rights become easier to change.
Planning authorities should check every building permit in full, without fast-track exemptions for new towns, farm homes or renovations, even if building takes much longer.
The law should close more gaps between women and men, such as pay, benefits and public budgets, even if employers and the state pay more.
The law should limit working hours more strictly, such as a shorter work week and capped shifts for medical interns, even if employers' costs rise.
Pay and benefits for public employees, such as firefighters and teachers, should not be raised, even if some of them leave for the private sector.
Local planning committees, not national planning bodies, should decide on building plans in their area, even if national housing and infrastructure projects move slower.
The state should direct more resources to low-income families and poorer towns, such as water discounts and housing grants, even if middle-income families get less.
Residents should pay less property tax (arnona) and parking charges, with discounts for groups like reservists and people with disabilities, even if municipalities cut services.
The state should provide free legal help to more people, such as victims of crime, terror or domestic violence, even if this costs the budget more.

166.name_en: Territory under Israeli sovereignty and law
166.plus_en: Applies Israeli sovereignty or law to more territory.
166.minus_en: Applies Israeli sovereignty or law to less territory.

171.plus_en: Permits more economic and other ties with hostile entities and states, or designates fewer of them as hostile.
171.minus_en: Restricts economic and other ties with hostile entities and states, or designates more of them as hostile (e.g. declaring a state an enemy state).

165a.name_en: Jewish character of the state in the Basic Laws
165a.plus_en: Anchors the state's Jewish identity more firmly in the Basic Laws (Basic Law: State of Israel, the Nation-State Law, loyalty oaths to a Jewish and democratic state, Zionism as a guiding value).
165a.minus_en: Weakens that anchoring: repeals the Nation-State Law or gives the Declaration of Independence and its equality principle Basic Law status.

164.name_en: State support for Jewish identity and the Diaspora
164.plus_en: Gives more state support to Jewish identity programs and Diaspora ties.

184.name_en: Powers to revoke citizenship and status
184.plus_en: Makes it easier to revoke citizenship or residency status.

185a.plus_en: Increases the conscription of yeshiva and Haredi men (enlistment quotas, sanctions, 'service for all', limiting Torah-study deferrals).
185a.minus_en: Expands or entrenches exemptions or deferrals for Torah study or religious reasons.

185b.name_en: Length and breadth of general conscription and reserve duty
185b.plus_en: Lengthens compulsory or reserve service, raises the exemption age, or extends conscription to more groups of the general population (e.g. new immigrants).
185b.minus_en: Shortens compulsory or reserve service, abolishes conscription, or adds individual exemptions (conscience, gender).

187.name_en: Linkage of rights and benefits to service
187.plus_en: Ties rights and benefits more strongly to military or national service.

179.name_en: Admission of foreigners for entry and residence
179.plus_en: Makes it easier for foreigners to enter and stay.
179.minus_en: Makes it harder for foreigners to enter and stay.

173.name_en: Activity of foreign states and international organizations inside Israel
173.plus_en: Allows foreign states or international organizations more physical presence or operations on Israeli territory.
173.minus_en: Restricts their presence or operations inside Israel.

180.plus_en: Allows more foreign workers or makes hiring them easier and cheaper.
180.minus_en: Allows fewer foreign workers or makes hiring them harder.

3.name_en: Benefits for soldiers, reservists and veterans
3.plus_en: Gives more benefits, payments and preferences to those who served and their families.
3.minus_en: Gives fewer benefits, payments and preferences to those who served and their families.

92b.name_en: Rights and conditions of security prisoners
92b.plus_en: Gives prisoners jailed for terrorism or security offences more rights or milder conditions (visits, phone, studies, early release).
92b.minus_en: Gives them fewer rights or harsher conditions.

255a.name_en: Funding of schools that do not teach the core curriculum
255a.plus_en: Gives schools that do not teach core subjects (math, English) more state funding or fewer conditions.
255a.minus_en: Cuts their funding or makes it conditional on teaching core subjects.

300.name_en: State control over NGOs and associations
300.plus_en: Adds oversight and disclosure requirements for NGOs and associations (including cults).

158.plus_en: Adds non-religious options for marriage and personal status.

71.plus_en: The judiciary and its leadership are more self-governing.
71.minus_en: The judiciary is subject to more external influence.

151c.plus_en: Allows or expands separation of men and women in state and municipal services, events, studies or transport.

154.name_en: Powers of religious institutions and courts
154.plus_en: Gives religious institutions more powers and monopoly, extends Rabbinate and state control over religious bodies, or widens religious courts' jurisdiction.
154.minus_en: Reduces these powers, control or jurisdiction.

356b.plus_en: Gives more money or benefits to public transport (fare discounts, free travel, more lines and services).

169a.plus_en: Increases state funding, planning, regularisation, services or security for settlements in Judea and Samaria.

275.plus_en: Gives more possibilities to withdraw pension savings.

204.name_en: LGBT rights and recognition of non-traditional families
204.plus_en: Gives LGBT people more rights and protection, or recognizes non-traditional families more.
204.minus_en: Gives fewer rights or less recognition.

25a.plus_en: Fewer barriers for imports and new competitors in concentrated consumer markets (food, banking, pharmacies, transport, car services, media, insurance).
25a.minus_en: Protection of incumbent firms and local producers from imports and new entrants.

178.plus_en: Adds measures and sanctions against terrorism and its financing.

77a.plus_en: Broader powers for police, prison service and security forces to arrest, detain, search, monitor and use force; fewer limits on them.
77a.minus_en: More limits and oversight on police force, searches and dispersal of protests.

340.plus_en: Gives appointment vetting committees a larger role.

90a.name_en: Procedural rights of suspects and defendants
90a.plus_en: Gives suspects and defendants more safeguards in arrest, questioning, trial and appeal (lawyer, recording, disclosure).

31a.plus_en: Gives more benefits, assistance or incentives to olim and for aliyah.

353.name_en: Mandatory protective terms in private contracts
353.plus_en: Adds mandatory terms protecting the weaker side in contracts between private parties (consumers, tenants, insured persons, borrowers).
353.minus_en: Removes such mandatory terms; the stronger side has more contractual freedom.

283a.plus_en: Hands public services or their staffing to private companies or organizations (outsourcing, vouchers, contract employment, privatization).
283a.minus_en: Keeps or returns public services to state bodies and direct public employment.

277a.name_en: Denial of benefits and rights as a sanction
277a.plus_en: Denies or revokes benefits, allowances, licenses or other state rights from people as a sanction: those involved in terror and their families, illegal residents or infiltrators, boycott supporters, convicted officials.
277a.minus_en: Restores such benefits or rights, or limits the state's power to deny them as a sanction.

146.plus_en: Protects privacy and personal data better.
146.minus_en: Protects privacy and personal data less.

101b1.name_en: Guardianship of parents accused of violence
101b1.plus_en: Keeps or eases guardianship and custody of parents charged with or convicted of violence in the family.
101b1.minus_en: Lets the state remove or restrict their guardianship.

231e.name_en: Confiscation of property of criminals and terrorists
231e.plus_en: Expands the state's power to confiscate or forfeit property, money or assets of criminals, criminal organizations or terrorists, or of their supporters.
231e.minus_en: Narrows or limits such confiscation or forfeiture powers, or adds protections for owners and third parties.

60.name_en: Political control over state bodies and appointments
60.plus_en: Ministers and the cabinet control more; appointing bodies are freer; oversight bodies, regulators, legal advisers and prosecutors depend more on politicians.
60.minus_en: State bodies, legal advisers and prosecutors become more independent; appointments are bound by criteria.

66a.name_en: Judicial review of laws and government
66a.plus_en: Courts review and can strike down more laws and government decisions.
66a.minus_en: Courts review less; the Knesset can override or shield laws from review.

103a.name_en: Immunity of elected officials from criminal proceedings
103a.plus_en: Grants or widens immunity of Knesset members, ministers, the prime minister or heads of local authorities, or bars, delays or requires approval for criminal investigation, arrest or indictment of them while in office.
103a.minus_en: Narrows such immunity or makes it easier to investigate, arrest or indict them while in office.

92c.name_en: Rights and conditions of ordinary prisoners and detainees
92c.plus_en: Gives criminal prisoners and detainees more rights or milder conditions (rehabilitation, health care, limits on shackling, living space).
92c.minus_en: Gives them fewer rights or harsher conditions.

66b2.plus_en: Gives judges more discretion in sentencing.
66b2.minus_en: Fixes minimum or mandatory punishments for crimes (other than the death penalty), limiting judges' discretion.

151b.name_en: Jewish religious rules in public institutions
151b.plus_en: Makes hospitals, army bases, state bodies or public places follow more Jewish religious rules (kashrut, no leavened bread on Passover, Shabbat).
151b.minus_en: Makes them follow fewer such rules.

231d.name_en: Jewish land rights in Judea and Samaria
231d.plus_en: Expands rights of Israelis/Jews to buy, hold or reclaim land in Judea and Samaria (repeal of Jordanian purchase ban, pre-1948 land restoration).

291.plus_en: Enshrines more rights in Basic Laws.

201.name_en: Representation of women in public bodies
201.plus_en: Increases women's representation in public bodies.

277d.name_en: Eligibility for unemployment benefits and support for young workers
277d.plus_en: More people qualify for unemployment or employment-support benefits (e.g. interns, young people, workers past retirement age), or conditions are relaxed.
277d.minus_en: Fewer people qualify or conditions become stricter.

277g1.name_en: General state support for students and pupils
277g1.plus_en: More state support for students and pupils (grants, free meals, tuition aid, fares).

69b.name_en: Appeals against decisions of public bodies
69b.plus_en: People get more ways to appeal or challenge decisions of police, health funds, benefit offices and other public bodies (reasons, records, appeal periods).

195a.name_en: Dismissal of public employees over support for terror
195a.plus_en: Makes it easier or mandatory to dismiss teachers, lecturers or public employees who express support for terror.
195a.minus_en: Makes such dismissal harder or removes it.

254.plus_en: Adds institutions or places in higher education.

170.name_en: Financial resources of the Palestinian Authority
170.plus_en: The Palestinian Authority receives more funds.
170.minus_en: The Palestinian Authority receives fewer funds (e.g. offsets, withholding).

277f.name_en: Eligibility for survivors' and bereaved families' benefits
277f.plus_en: More widows, widowers, orphans or bereaved families qualify for survivors' or bereavement benefits, or conditions are relaxed (e.g. widow who remarried keeps the benefit).
277f.minus_en: Fewer qualify or conditions become stricter (e.g. family recognition revoked).

28.plus_en: Gives farmers more benefits and grants.
28.minus_en: Gives farmers fewer benefits and grants.

117b.name_en: Voting access for people away from home
117b.plus_en: Makes voting easier for people away from home or with limited mobility (soldiers, students, absentee and accessible polling).

12b.plus_en: Health funds and providers owe patients more services and rights (treatment times, refunds, coverage).

106.name_en: Powers and autonomy of local government
106.plus_en: Gives municipalities more powers and freedom.
106.minus_en: Gives municipalities fewer powers and less freedom.

277b.name_en: Eligibility for disability, nursing-care and sickness benefits
277b.plus_en: More people qualify for disability, nursing-care, sickness or rehabilitation benefits, or conditions are relaxed (e.g. means test removed).
277b.minus_en: Fewer people qualify or conditions become stricter.

144.plus_en: Adds environmental requirements and nature protection, or gives environmental authorities more influence.
144.minus_en: Reduces environmental requirements or the influence of environmental authorities.

226.plus_en: Gives creditors more debt-collection tools, stronger insolvency rights or more and longer-held information about borrowers.
226.minus_en: Gives creditors fewer such tools, rights or information.

80a.name_en: Independent state inquiry into security failures
80a.plus_en: Security failures are investigated by an independent state commission of inquiry.
80a.minus_en: Inquiry is avoided or run by a body chosen by politicians.

98.name_en: Coercive measures against persons under protective orders
98.plus_en: Imposes more measures and obligations on persons subject to protective orders.

277e.name_en: Eligibility for old-age benefits and benefits for Holocaust survivors
277e.plus_en: More senior citizens or Holocaust survivors qualify for pensions, allowances or exemptions, or conditions are relaxed (e.g. means test removed, eligibility age lowered).
277e.minus_en: Fewer qualify or conditions become stricter.

253a.plus_en: Expands free public educational services, from early childhood to after-school programmes and higher education.

124a.plus_en: Lets a prime minister serve longer or removes limits.
124a.minus_en: Limits how long a person may serve as prime minister.

58b.name_en: Checks on the prime minister's power
58b.plus_en: Gives the prime minister more freedom to act alone (appoint or dismiss senior officials and ministers, refuse a state inquiry, decide without referendum or approval).
58b.minus_en: Limits that freedom or adds checks on it.

117a.name_en: Who has the right to vote
117a.plus_en: Keeps or widens the right to vote (no service or other conditions).
117a.minus_en: Conditions or removes the right to vote (military or national service, prisoners).

162s2.plus_en: Obliges or allows the state, employers, landlords and public bodies to accommodate observant Jews: Shabbat mechanisms in buildings, prayer and religious conditions for prisoners and soldiers, religious exemptions or tracks in military service, gender-separated bathing, events or study tracks, Jewish prayer at holy sites, free parking on Shabbat, protection from offending religious belief.
162s2.minus_en: Removes or narrows such accommodations and religious exemptions.

251s3.name_en: Qualification and criminal-record requirements for staff working with children and vulnerable people
251s3.plus_en: Requires training or qualifications for daycare, kindergarten, school and care staff, or bars people convicted or accused of sexual or violent offences from working in education, childcare, academia, medicine or therapy.
251s3.minus_en: Relaxes such qualification or vetting requirements (e.g. lets older or less qualified people work as caregivers or foster parents).

100c.name_en: Broadcasting court hearings and public meetings
100c.plus_en: Requires filming or broadcasting of court hearings, council meetings or other public proceedings.

271a.plus_en: Keeps or adds restrictions on cannabis.
271a.minus_en: Legalises or decriminalises cannabis for personal or medical use.

80b.name_en: Checks on police use of force
80b.plus_en: Stricter checks on police use of force (filming, body cameras, complaint handling, protest-dispersal rules).

99s2.name_en: Safety and supervision of children's care, schooling and surroundings
99s2.plus_en: Adds safety and supervision requirements where children are cared for, taught or transported: daycare licensing and inspection, cameras, vetting and dismissal of staff accused or convicted of abuse, school security and anti-bullying duties, protected spaces, traffic safety near schools and devices against leaving children in cars, dangerous toys and pools.
99s2.minus_en: Removes or relaxes such safety and supervision requirements for children's institutions and surroundings.

22s3.name_en: Protection of residents removed from their homes by redevelopment or building hazards
22s3.plus_en: Guarantees compensation, rehousing or conditions before residents are evicted from long-held urban neighbourhoods (e.g. Kfar Shalem, Givat Amal, Abu Kabir) or removed for demolition, structural reinforcement or collapse danger, including protection of elderly residents and of apartment owners in urban-renewal deals.
22s3.minus_en: Reduces such compensation, rehousing or conditions, making it easier to remove residents.

12a.name_en: Ban on conversion therapy for minors
12a.plus_en: Bans or restricts therapy aimed at changing a minor's sexual orientation.

322.plus_en: Tightens requirements for candidates for judgeships.

110s3.plus_en: Requires or lengthens cooling-off periods before senior officials, regulators, judges, security officers or politicians may move to the private sector, lobbying, politics or another senior post, or from the private sector into the civil service.
110s3.minus_en: Shortens or removes such cooling-off periods.

99s1.name_en: Criminal-law protection of minors from abuse
99s1.plus_en: Toughens criminal law on violence and sexual offences against minors: harsher or minimum penalties, new offences, longer or abolished limitation periods, wider mandatory reporting, easier investigation and testimony of child victims, offender registries and monitoring.
99s1.minus_en: Softens such criminal law: milder penalties, shorter limitation periods, fewer reporting duties or fewer special procedures for child victims.

85.name_en: Criminal bans on incitement and hate
85.plus_en: Covers more groups and acts under incitement and hate prohibitions.

279s2.name_en: Dedicated state bodies for social, health and welfare problems
279s2.plus_en: Creates a state authority, commission, committee, centre or official post dedicated to a social, health or welfare problem or a vulnerable group (poverty, suicide prevention, trauma and mental health, early childhood, domestic violence, families of missing persons, women's status, people with disabilities, senior citizens, children).
279s2.minus_en: Abolishes or merges such dedicated bodies or posts, or leaves the problem to general ministries without a dedicated body.

160s1.plus_en: Adds protection and remedies for victims of violence within the family: a wider definition of domestic violence (economic, psychological), easier and longer protective orders and their electronic enforcement, harsher penalties and abolished limitation periods for sexual offences in the family, treatment centres and a national authority, protection of the home and rights of children whose parent was killed by the other parent, loss of marital property rights by a spouse who murdered the other.
160s1.minus_en: Reduces such protection or remedies for victims of domestic violence.

19s3.name_en: Non-discrimination in access to goods, services and public places
19s3.plus_en: Adds grounds or situations in which businesses, landlords, schools and places open to the public may not discriminate or segregate customers (e.g. by gender, ethnic origin, appearance, family status, disability, breastfeeding, refusal to give personal data), or makes such bans easier to enforce.
19s3.minus_en: Removes grounds or situations covered by such bans, or allows service providers to refuse, separate or treat customers differently.

110s2.name_en: Barring candidates and office holders over support for terror or enemies
110s2.plus_en: Bars from running for or holding Knesset, local-council, ministerial or other public office, or removes from it, people who support armed struggle or terror against Israel, back an enemy state during conflict, were convicted of terror, or refuse a loyalty declaration.
110s2.minus_en: Repeals or narrows such grounds for disqualification or removal (e.g. cancelling the procedure for ending an MK's membership).

22s2.plus_en: Widens who is entitled to public housing or strengthens tenants' rights in it: continuing-tenant rights for family members, eligibility for single mothers receiving child support and for women leaving shelters, improvements in the apartments.
22s2.minus_en: Narrows eligibility for public housing or tenants' rights in it.

251s2.name_en: Licensing and entry exams for non-health professions and trades
251s2.plus_en: Brings more non-health occupations and service providers under licensing or tightens their entry requirements: bar exams and internship for lawyers, accountants, notaries, tax representatives, mortgage and financial advisers, insurance appraisers, technicians, sports coaches, dog trainers, mediators, security firms, manpower contractors, car-service businesses.
251s2.minus_en: Removes licensing for such occupations or eases entry: lower pass marks or shorter internships, recognition of foreign licences, fast-track licensing, letting other licensed professionals (e.g. lawyers, pension advisers) do the work.

9.plus_en: Raises fees and tariffs citizens pay for public services.
9.minus_en: Lowers such fees or makes the services free.

163p2.plus_en: More state money and discounts for yeshivas, Haredi schools, religious councils, houses of prayer and holy sites
163p2.minus_en: Less state funding and fewer discounts for religious institutions and schools

11s2.name_en: Health facilities and services in peripheral localities
11s2.plus_en: Requires or funds hospitals, emergency rooms, medical equipment or lower health-insurance contributions specifically in peripheral, border or minority localities (e.g. Kiryat Shmona, Sderot, Netivot, Dimona, Eilat, Sakhnin), or obliges the health system to close gaps between the periphery and the centre.
11s2.minus_en: Reduces or removes such region-specific health facilities, funding or obligations.

17s2.name_en: Anti-discrimination and representation duties of private organizations
17s2.plus_en: Requires businesses, employers, educational institutions and other private organizations to avoid discrimination (by gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, ethnicity, economic status, place of residence) or to ensure adequate representation of women, people with disabilities, Arab or Haredi citizens and residents of the periphery (e.g. board quotas, hiring targets, conditions in tenders, pay-transparency duties).
17s2.minus_en: Removes or relaxes such anti-discrimination, representation or pay-transparency duties for private organizations.

162s3.name_en: Religious practice of Muslims and other non-Jewish communities
162s3.plus_en: Gives Muslim, Christian, Druze and other non-Jewish believers more room to practice: prayer rooms in hospitals, a shorter working day in Ramadan, study adjustments for their holidays, development of Muslim holy places; fewer limits on the call to prayer or on religious outreach.
162s3.minus_en: Restricts such practice: limits on the muezzin's call to prayer, bans on proselytizing, fewer accommodations.

256s4.name_en: Jewish and national heritage, commemoration and symbols in schools
256s4.plus_en: Requires schools and universities to teach Jewish and Israeli history and the heritage of specific Jewish communities, to mark commemoration days or run memorial programs (e.g. October 7), or to display the national flag and use the anthem.
256s4.minus_en: Removes or reduces such mandatory heritage teaching, commemoration and national symbols in education.

134.plus_en: Permits more speech, assembly and protest.
134.minus_en: Prohibits more speech or restricts assembly and protest.

99s3.name_en: Shielding minors from harmful content and products
99s3.plus_en: Restricts minors' access or exposure to harmful content and consumer products: internet filtering, age verification and age limits on social networks, removal of harmful online content, bans on selling or advertising tobacco, energy drinks, nitrous oxide, cannabis, gambling machines or toy weapons to or near minors.
99s3.minus_en: Lifts such restrictions; minors and their families decide for themselves what content and products to use.

11s3.plus_en: Gives more people state-funded psychological or psychiatric treatment and trauma care: soldiers, reservists and their families, people with combat stress or PTSD, victims of terror, war and sexual or family violence, children and youth with mental difficulties, mothers with postpartum depression; creates crisis-intervention teams or a national trauma authority.
11s3.minus_en: Reduces such state-funded mental-health and trauma care or narrows who receives it.

89s2.name_en: Ethics, disclosure and reporting duties of ministers and Knesset members
89s2.plus_en: Imposes more ethics rules, disclosure or reporting duties on ministers, Knesset members and party leaders (external advisers, foreign ties and accounts, securities trading, coalition agreements and coalition funds, missed deadlines for regulations or the budget), or gives ethics bodies more powers over them.
89s2.minus_en: Removes or relaxes such ethics, disclosure and reporting duties, or reduces the powers of ethics bodies over them.

290s1.name_en: Representation of Arab citizens in public bodies
290s1.plus_en: Guarantees Arab, Druze or Circassian citizens seats or adequate representation in planning bodies, municipalities, the civil service, government companies, sports bodies and other public bodies.

279s1.name_en: Number of political offices in national and local government
279s1.plus_en: Adds or allows more ministers, deputy ministers, additional ministers within one ministry, an alternate prime minister, or more (including paid) deputy heads of local authorities.
279s1.minus_en: Caps the number of ministers and deputy ministers, abolishes or merges ministries, abolishes the alternate (rotation) government, or limits the number of deputy heads of local authorities.

81s3.name_en: Penalties for violent, sexual and property crime
81s3.plus_en: Adds offences or harsher punishments for ordinary (non-security) crime: violence and sexual offences, including against minors, partners, the elderly and helpless persons; assaults on workers who serve the public (medical staff, bus drivers, lawyers, social workers, police officers, journalists); prostitution and human trafficking; organized crime, protection rackets, illegal weapons, agricultural crime, theft and looting.
81s3.minus_en: Removes such offences or makes their punishment milder.

317s2.name_en: Priority for senior citizens, people with disabilities and parents of infants in everyday services
317s2.plus_en: Gives senior citizens, people with disabilities, pregnant women or parents with infants priority in queues, a human answer on telephone service lines, or reserved or free parking.

156.plus_en: Creates more routes to recognized conversion (giyur).

22s1.name_en: Rights of tenants in the private rental market
22s1.plus_en: Strengthens renters and long-term lessees against landlords: limits on rent increases, the landlord rather than the tenant pays the broker's fee, longer leases or lease extensions during emergencies, renewal of long-term leases.
22s1.minus_en: Weakens renters and lessees against landlords: freer rent setting, the tenant bears the broker's fee, shorter or no lease protection.

75.plus_en: Guarantees the opposition more seats and powers.
75.minus_en: Guarantees the opposition fewer seats and powers.

96s3.plus_en: Raises compensation, fines or funding cuts for those who discriminate in services, education, housing or employment, or who publish racist content.

248s1.plus_en: Adds restrictions on tobacco and smoking products: advertising and flavor bans, content limits, sales limits, smoke-free places, higher tobacco tax.

240s1.plus_en: Strengthens enforcement against building without a permit: demolitions, penalties, bans on connecting unlicensed buildings to utilities, or measures against unlicensed construction in Area C.
240s1.minus_en: Limits demolitions and penalties for unlicensed construction, freezes enforcement, or regularizes unlicensed housing (e.g. in minority localities or on grazing land).

270.name_en: Explicit consent requirement for posthumous use
270.plus_en: Tightens explicit-consent requirements for posthumous use (e.g. organs, gametes).

1s1.name_en: Level of social-security and welfare cash benefits
1s1.plus_en: Raises social-security and welfare cash benefits (national insurance allowances, income support, work grant, foster-care payments, burial and death grants, benefits for Holocaust survivors and other groups) or widens who receives them.
1s1.minus_en: Lowers such benefits or narrows who receives them (e.g. cuts in budget-arrangements laws).

309s3.plus_en: Widens who may adopt and removes obstacles in adoption: adoption by single parents or by couples (including same-sex couples), removal or narrowing of the requirement that adopters share the child's religion, keeping siblings together, revised suitability criteria.
309s3.minus_en: Narrows who may adopt or adds conditions on adopters (e.g. keeps or tightens the same-religion requirement).

276.plus_en: Increases state support for pension savings.

292.name_en: Entrenchment and supremacy of Basic Laws
292.plus_en: Makes Basic Laws harder to amend or gives them more precedence.
292.minus_en: Makes them easier to amend or gives them less precedence.

240s3.plus_en: Adds conditions, approvals or procedural steps for obtaining building permits and approving plans.
240s3.minus_en: Speeds up or simplifies building permits and plan approval: exemptions, fast-track procedures, relief for existing buildings, urban renewal, apartment splitting, temporary uses.

202.plus_en: Reduces differences in how the law treats women and men, or adds rights specifically for women.
202.minus_en: Increases legal differences between women and men to women's disadvantage, or removes women-specific rights. Gender-neutral rules do not count.

209a.plus_en: Lengthens or allows longer working time (longer week, longer shifts).
209a.minus_en: Shortens working time by law (shorter week, caps on shifts, e.g. for medical interns).

215.name_en: Pay and status of public sector employees
215.plus_en: Raises pay and status of public employees.

244.name_en: Centralization of land-use and building planning
244.plus_en: Moves more land-use, zoning or building-plan approval authority to national or central planning bodies (away from local and district planning committees).
244.minus_en: Moves land-use, zoning or building-plan approval authority from national or central bodies to local or district planning committees.

377.name_en: Redistribution toward low-income groups and poor areas
377.plus_en: Shifts resources specifically toward low-income people or poor localities (means-tested or socio-economic criteria).
377.minus_en: Shifts resources away from them, or removes socio-economic targeting.

311s1.name_en: State-funded legal aid and court costs for individuals
311s1.plus_en: Widens who receives state-funded legal aid or lowers what individuals pay to go to court: legal aid for victims of sexual offences, domestic violence, fraud, hostile acts and other crimes, for nursing-care patients and for plaintiffs in discrimination or civil cases, state funding of experts, guardians' fees and family-court proceedings, exemptions from court fees, longer or extended legal-aid temporary provisions.
311s1.minus_en: Narrows who receives state-funded legal aid or raises what individuals pay to go to court (e.g. denies legal aid to husbands who refuse to grant a divorce).
